chunks: Rijal al-Kashshi: Hamduwayh from al-Hasan ibn Musa al-Khashab from Ibrahim ibn Abi Mahmud who said:

I entered upon Abi Ja'far (peace be upon him) and with me were letters to him from his father, so he began reading them and placing the larger letters upon his eyes and saying: 'The handwriting of my father – by Allah,' and crying until his tears reached his cheeks, so I said to him: 'May I be your ransom, your father would sometimes say to me in a single sitting numerous times: May Allah lodge you in Paradise, may Allah make you enter Paradise.' He said: So he said: 'And I also say: May Allah make you enter Paradise.' Then I said: 'May I be your ransom, do you guarantee for me from your Lord that you will make me enter Paradise?' He said: 'Yes.' He said: So I took his leg and kissed it.

key_terms.جَعَلْتُ فَدَاكَ: May I be your ransom (a phrase of deep respect)

ai.seo_question: What is the story of Ibrahim ibn Abi Mahmud and Imam al-Jawad's promise of Paradise?
ai.summary: This narration from Al-Kashi’s *Rijal* highlights the deep emotional bond between the Imams and their forebears, illustrating how the Imam al-Jawad’s tears were not merely for grief but for the spiritual weight of his father’s promises. The dialogue underscores the Shia concept of *Kafalah* (guarantee) by the Imam, where the Imam’s word serves as a divine assurance of Paradise for the faithful, a privilege Ibrahim sought and received through the intimate act of kissing the Imam’s leg.
